Let \(q=\ell\), and write
\[
v(x)=\chi(1+x)\qquad (x\in H).
\]
For \(\varepsilon\in\{1,-1\}\), expand
\[
\sum_{a\in\mathbb F_q^\times} C_{+1}(a)C_{\varepsilon}(a)
=
\sum_{x,y\in H} v(x)v(y)
\sum_{a\in\mathbb F_q^\times}\chi(1+ax)\chi(1+\varepsilon ay).
\]

We need the inner sum. For nonzero \(\alpha,\beta\),
\[
\sum_{a\in\mathbb F_q}\chi((1+\alpha a)(1+\beta a))
=
\begin{cases}
q-1,&\alpha=\beta,\\
-\chi(\alpha\beta),&\alpha\ne\beta,
\end{cases}
\]
because in the distinct-root case this is the quadratic character sum of a nonconstant quadratic with leading coefficient \(\alpha\beta\). Removing the \(a=0\) term subtracts \(1\).

For \(\varepsilon=1\), since \(x,y\in H\), \(\chi(xy)=1\). Thus the inner sum is \(q-2\) if \(x=y\), and \(-2\) if \(x\ne y\). Therefore
\[
\sum_{a\ne0}C_{+1}(a)^2
=
-2\left(\sum_{x\in H}v(x)\right)^2
+q\sum_{x\in H}v(x)^2.
\]
Now \(-1\notin H\) because \(q\equiv3\pmod4\), so \(1+x\ne0\) for all \(x\in H\), hence
\[
\sum_{x\in H}v(x)^2=|H|=r=\frac{q-1}{2}.
\]
Also
\[
\sum_{x\in H}\chi(1+x)
=
\frac12\sum_{x\ne0}(1+\chi(x))\chi(1+x).
\]
Here
\[
\sum_{x\ne0}\chi(1+x)=-1,
\]
and
\[
\sum_{x\ne0}\chi(x)\chi(1+x)
=
\sum_{x\in\mathbb F_q}\chi(x(x+1))=-1,
\]
since \(x(x+1)\) is a quadratic with two distinct roots. Hence
\[
\sum_{x\in H}v(x)=-1.
\]
So
\[
\sum_{a\ne0}C_{+1}(a)^2
=
q\frac{q-1}{2}-2.
\]

For \(\varepsilon=-1\), the inner sum is
\[
\sum_{a\ne0}\chi((1+ax)(1-ay)).
\]
The two roots would coincide only if \(y=-x\), impossible because \(x,y\in H\) and \(-1\notin H\). Its leading coefficient is \(-xy\), whose character is \(-1\). Thus the full sum over \(a\in\mathbb F_q\) is \(-\chi(-xy)=1\), and after subtracting the \(a=0\) term, the inner sum is \(0\). Therefore
\[
\sum_{a\ne0}C_{+1}(a)C_{-1}(a)=0.
\]

Thus the ordered pair is
\[
\boxed{\left(\frac{\ell(\ell-1)}2-2,\;0\right)}.
\]
